newsitem.title: USA: US stocks dip, hit by rising bond yields, programs.
newsitem.headline: US stocks dip, hit by rising bond yields, programs.

text.p: Stock prices closed lower Thursday as Wall Street's nerves were again rattled by rising long-term interest rates in the bond market ahead of next week's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting arm.
Worries about the quality of second-quarter corporate profits also cut into stocks, analysts said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell unofficially 36 points to 7654. It was the fourth day this week that stocks were subject to sharp swings.

The approach of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting next week only added to the jitters, analysts said, although most economists are not expecting a credit tightening until the policy panel's August meeting.
Despite the volatility, Bleier said he was still bullish.
"You have to take these sell-offs with a grain of salt. We are taking a pause, but the fundamental macroeconomic backdrop remains unchanged," he said.

Disk drive makers slumped after San Jose, California-based Komag Inc said profits for the second quarter and the rest of the year would fall short of Wall Street expectations. The stock, the most heavily traded on the Nasdaq, dropped 6-7/8 to 16-11/16. Rivals Seagate Technology and Read-Rite Corp also slumped.
Technology and drug stocks, which have led the market higher, were weaker. Pharmacia & Upjohn, Johnson & Johnson, Warner-Lambert Co and Pfizer all closed lower.
Among blue-chip technology stocks, International Business Machines Corp, Micron Technology Inc, Compaq Computer Corp and Intel Corp all closed lower.

Bucking the trend, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc shares surged 11-9/16 to 91 after its French parent, Rhone-Poulenc SA, said it was considering a $4.3 billion bid to buy the rest of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer it does not own.
Decliners beat advancers 1,455 to 1,300 on the New York Stock Exchange, with volume reaching 499.8 million shares.
